one_month_reasoning: No CoreWeave earnings fall inside the window: no Q3 date is announced, and results are expected around Nov 5-16 [24]. In-window events: (1) supply from the 35M-share ATM [5] and weekly insider 10b5-1 sales [6], a mild negative; (2) hedging flows around the $97.85 convert strike [4]; (3) hyperscaler Q3 earnings and 2027 capex commentary (GOOGL/META ~Oct 28, AMZN ~Oct 29, MSFT late Oct; estimated dates), the main two-sided event; (4) the FOMC on Oct 27-28. Sell-side moves in late September (JPM upgrade to OW/$125 on Sep 24 [28]; Redburn Sell/$54 on Sep 21 [29]) are already in the $88.57 close. The supervisor confirmed this event set and none of its corrections bears on a one-month view, so the ladder was unchanged in round 2: near-symmetric at ~26% monthly vol (93%/3.5) with a slight tilt below spot for dilution supply. Round 3: the GPU-life research changes long-run unit economics, not anything that reprices in the next four weeks. No GPU-price print or contract roll in the window is scheduled to force the issue (CME/Silicon Data compute futures launch on Oct 5 [34] adds a public price signal, which I treat as two-sided). The 1-month ladder is unchanged. Round 4: the site inventory and the split discount rate change long-run value, not anything priced in the next four weeks. The only in-window site event, Applied Digital's remaining 75 MW going live on Oct 2, was already scheduled. The 1-month ladder is unchanged.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of a site-reconciled vintage DCF with split discounting ($4.6: signed in-term contract cash at 8.6%, everything else at 11.5%; 5-yr contracts then 50%/41% re-lease, 6-yr base life, 25% fixed site cost, SBC deducted; unfloored base cell $-74, floored grid $4.6) and 5.2x Oct-27 NTM adj. EBITDA of $20.3B ($69). Each cohort at 2.6x capex still earns below WACC, so the DCF is positive only on the tight re-contracting path.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Vintage model at 2027-10-01, rebuilt so every inventory site appears once. Energized (<=2026 cohorts, 1.85 GW), contracted under construction (2027 cohort ~1.13 GW, 2028 cohort ~1.23 GW), self-builds probability-weighted, pipeline probability-weighted (land 1.5 GW at 0.5, NVIDIA gap 2.3 GW at 0.2), exited sites removed. 5-yr contracts at contract price, then 50%/41%; fixed site cost 25% (was 28%) + 13% variable; SBC 5%->3%; maintenance 1.5%/yr; refresh 2.3x; growth 2.6x. Signed in-term cash (62.5% of <=2027 cohorts, 31% of 2028, x performance 95/90/85%) at 8.6%; the rest at WACC 11.5%; g 3%. Net debt $64.4B (incl. $1.37B JV commitments), 620M shares. Unfloored base cell $-74.2 (single-rate $-77.1); floored grid $4.6 (single-rate $4.0).

inputs_detail.input: Capacity and run-rate path by site category
inputs_detail.value: <=2026 cohorts $19B run-rate (1.85 GW energized); 2027 adds $11.5B (~1.13 GW); 2028 adds $13.0B (~1.23 GW), reaching ~4.2 GW contracted; 2029 adds $15.5B x P0.5 (PIPE-LAND); 2030 adds $23.7B x P0.2 (NVIDIA gap to 8 GW); then 3% growth
inputs_detail.derivation: Round 3 used $13B/$13B/$12B adds for 2028-30 at full weight. The inventory shows 4.2 GW contracted (8/11/26) against 1.5 GW active; at ~$10.3M of run-rate per MW (exit-2026 $19B / 1.85 GW) the 2027-28 adds fill the 4.2 GW. Beyond that only 1.5 GW of land/options/LOIs is identified, and the NVIDIA framework overlaps the 8 GW target, so the 2029-30 adds are probability-weighted (see PIPE rows in site_coverage).
Unchanged: weighted-average contract length on new capacity ~5 yrs [36].

inputs_detail.input: Signed share of in-term cash flows
inputs_detail.value: 62.5% for <=2027 cohorts, 31% for 2028; ~$80B of signed revenue remaining at 2027-10-01 out of ~$157B modelled in-term revenue
inputs_detail.derivation: RPO $103.7B at 6/30/26 [2] less ~$22B to be recognised Jul-26 to Sep-27 leaves ~$80B (the >$25B of Q3 3-6-month commitments [63] run off before Oct-27). Mix of that $80B: Meta ~$34B, NVIDIA backstop ~$6B, Microsoft ~$4B (IG, ~55%); Jane Street ~$5.5B (~7%); OpenAI ~$16B, Anthropic ~$5B, others ~$9.5B (unrated, ~38%). Contracted power (4.2 GW) is not contracted revenue: only about half of the in-term cash the model assumes is signed today. That is a skeptic finding.

inputs_detail.value: 8.6% blended: IG (Meta Aa3, NVIDIA Aa1, Microsoft Aaa) 8.0%; Jane Street (BBB-/Ba1/BB) 8.75%; unrated (OpenAI, Anthropic, other) 9.5%
inputs_detail.derivation: Anchor: DDTL 4.0, the secured, non-recourse loan against the IG contract, prices at ~5.9% fixed (2.00% over the ~3-yr Treasury of 3.81% on 3/31/26) [47]. The 3-yr Treasury is now 4.91% [20], so the same loan today costs ~6.9%. The loan covers ~83% of contract-cash value (1.2x DSCR); the ~17% first-loss residual carries completion and operating risk at ~13%. 0.83 x 6.9% + 0.17 x 13% = ~7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. Unrated: the OpenAI-backed DDTL 3.0 costs SOFR+400 (~8.1%), and its 2025-12-31 amendment shows delivery slippage; with the same residual, ~9.1%, plus 0.4% for concentration = 9.5%. Jane Street is IG only at Fitch, so in between at 8.75%. Weighted by the signed mix: 8.6%.

inputs_detail.value: Year 6 at 50% of contract price; year 7 at 41%; retired after
inputs_detail.derivation: Unchanged from round 3. The fact-check confirms the inputs I used: H100 index $2.79 in Jul-25 then $2.80-2.90 to Apr-26 (not $2.80-2.84; immaterial), A100 23-39% of launch, re-booking 'within 5%' (confirmed via Intrator's post). Tight path (re-contract at 95%, then 0.78/0.64/0.53/0.44, 10-yr life) kept at 20% weight.

inputs_detail.input: Fixed site cost (lease + power + site ops)
inputs_detail.derivation: The inventory gives CoreWeave's actual lease costs: ~$1.44M/MW-yr (Core Scientific), ~$1.8M (Applied Digital), ~$1.9M (Galaxy), ~$2.2M (Blockfusion LOI). Plus power ~$0.5-0.7M/MW-yr and ~$0.2M site ops gives ~$2.5M/MW-yr, or ~24-25% of ~$10.3M run-rate per MW. Q2-26 cost of revenue (34% [35]) is inflated by capacity not yet billing, as the supervisor noted. Effect: +$26/share in the base cell.

inputs_detail.value: 6 years (5 contracted + 1 tail); 5y and 7y sensitivities; grid weights 5y 20% / 6y 40% / 7y 20% / tight 20%
inputs_detail.derivation: At 25% fixed cost the keep-while-cash-positive rule gives 7 yrs (year-7 net ~0.06, year-8 negative), as it did at 28%. I keep 6 as the base: it matches CoreWeave's 6-yr book life, which the fact-check confirms (Nebius 5 from 1 Jan 2026, IREN 5).

inputs_detail.value: 1.5%/yr of capex from year 4; refresh 2.3x (IT only, 0.885k); growth 2.6x (grid 2.4/2.6/2.7x)
inputs_detail.derivation: Unchanged. Self-build shells (Kenilworth, Hammond) are charged separately because k is equipment-based.

inputs_detail.value: +$2.2B Kenilworth (P0.9), +$0.7B Hammond (P0.75): avoided lease $1.8M/MW-yr less $0.25M owner O&M for 20 yrs, less remaining shell capex ($0.7B / $1.2B); capacity probability-weighted at WACC (-$0.37B vs full weight)
inputs_detail.derivation: Flag F4. ~$1.8B project for up to 250 MW (~$7.2M/MW shell) [62]; the lease rate avoided is taken from the APLD/Galaxy leases.

inputs_detail.value: Net debt +$1.37B (JV-2 remaining $1.22B, NJ JV remaining $0.10B, expected $0.02B guarantee call); JV stakes valued at 0.8x cost (+$1.48B)
inputs_detail.derivation: 10-Q: up to $1.7B committed, $479M carrying; NJ JV max funding $160M, $57M contributed, $95M guarantee. The 0.8x haircut reflects developer equity funded below a 9% parent cost (judgment).

inputs_detail.value: Performance probabilities 95% (energized), 90% (2027), 85% (2028); failure moves the signed share to WACC and costs ~1 yr of that EBITDA (-$0.97B total)
inputs_detail.derivation: Flag F9: Poolside's 250 MW (+500 MW) was terminated in Apr-26, Helios II slipped ~1 yr, and the DDTL 3.0 amendment pushed DSCR tests 'to align with delivery schedule'. These are base rates for slippage rather than permanent loss, because the GPUs were redeployed.

inputs_detail.value: In the runoff floor, lease (17.5% of contract revenue) continues to age 14 after retirement, discounted at 9%: 6-yr runoff -$15 -> -$62/share
inputs_detail.derivation: 12-15-yr leases (weighted remaining 12 yrs; $29.1B undiscounted commenced) outlive 6-yr GPU cohorts. The full model refreshes each slot at 2.3x, so leases stay covered. The runoff case shows that refresh is forced: stopping investment strands ~$47/share of rent.

inputs_detail.value: SBC 5%->3% of revenue deducted; WACC 11.5%; g 3%; NOLs ~$8B then 21%; 620M shares
Base cell (6y, 2.6x) unfloored: split $-74.2, single $-77.1. 5y/7y/tight at 2.6x split: $-101.7/$-72.1/$19.3. Floored grid: split $4.6, single $4.0. Unfloored grid mean: split $-55.5, single $-58.3
inputs_detail.derivation: Bridge from round 3 (-$128.9, base cell): fixed cost 28->25% +$26.5; pipeline probability-weighted +$22.7 (growth earns below WACC, so less of it is worth more); JV/self-build/failure/net-debt items +$2.6; split rate +$2.9 = -$74.2. Only the tight-path cells are positive ($10-38). The split rate adds ~0.14 of NPV per $ of signed run-rate, inside the supervisor's 0.10-0.15, but signed cash is only ~$36B of PV against $64B of net debt.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 5.2x x Oct-27 NTM adj. EBITDA $20.3B = EV $105.6B, less net debt $63B, less JV commitments $1.37B, plus JV stakes $1.48B = $42.7B over 620M shares = $69

inputs_detail.derivation: NTM revenue ~$34.2B: Q4'27 ~$7.4B at the ~$30B exit run-rate, plus Q1-Q3'28 ~$26.8B from the DCF path ($37B in 2028), at a ~59.5% margin (Q2 59%). This is close to the supervisor's ~$20.3B on consensus $26.3B. Round 1 reached a higher NTM figure only through an inconsistent margin path.

Same construction: installed-asset value plus half of today's growth premium. Installed value is rebuilt with the split rate and the 25% cost: the 5-yr contracted annuity is 3.79x (51% signed at 8.6% = 3.93x, the rest at 11.5% = 3.64x), plus tails of 0.14x (yr 6) and 0.04x (yr 7) = ~4.0x. Today's ~6.4x less 4.0x leaves a 2.4x growth premium; half is 1.2x, so 5.2x. On the supervisor's challenge: the market pays 6.4x today on ~90% NTM growth, and by Oct-27 growth roughly halves. The 6.0x consensus multiple ($95 with these bridges) is my sensitivity, not my base.
Same roll-forward as round 3, plus the off-balance-sheet JV items (flag F5).

bear.story: Rubin volume and new power capacity normalize GPU rental prices along the historical path (-50% within ~2 years of the next generation, then a flat floor). The 2023-24 Hopper cohorts re-contract at ~50% of original price in 2028-29, not ~95%. The market then values CRWV on its unit economics: at 2.6x capex, 5-yr contracts earn ~2-3% unlevered, below the cost of ~$20-25B of 2027 external funding at ~9%+. Add a customer cut (Customer A 40% of H1-26 revenue [2]) or a CDS move back above ~855bp [27], and equity trades as a thin option over ~$63B of net debt. Site lens: only ~half of the in-term cash on the 4.2 GW is signed today. A 2027 slip like Helios II or a Poolside-style exit would leave 12-15-yr leases running ahead of revenue (runoff floor -$62/share once stranded rent is counted).

base.story: Management's run-rate path holds (~$30B exit-2027, >3 GW active). Pricing stays firm through 2027 because power stays scarce (A100 into 2029 [37], H100 re-booked near original price [38]), so the decay question is not tested inside 12 months. Still, the multiple compresses from ~6.4x toward ~5-5.5x as investors price 5-yr contract terms against 6-yr book lives, Amazon-style life cuts [42] and the ATM/convert dilution. The IG-backed contracts (Meta ~$35B, NVIDIA backstop) and DDTL 4.0-style financing at ~7% keep funding open, which supports a multiple slightly above my round-3 view (5.2x).

bull.story: The tight-market regime persists. Older GPUs keep re-contracting near original prices (the H100 and A100 evidence [37][38]), which supports 9-10 yr cash lives and a positive DCF. Deliveries beat >3 GW, spreads compress, and the stock re-rates toward the ~$139-142 consensus target [18]. Convert dilution above $97.85 caps some of the upside.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$48 (21% under the $60.55 July low; ~$30B of equity at 620M shares against ~$45-48B of early-2027 net debt, ~4.5-5x NTM EBITDA), the move would most likely mean the funding or demand side has broken. Candidates: a punitive or failed DDTL/HY raise, CDS back above ~855bp, a Customer A cut, or a visible collapse in Hopper re-contract pricing. I move from $52 to the supervisor's $48 because the rebuilt DCF puts unit-economics fair value near zero. A slide into the low $50s can therefore happen through a multiple de-rating alone, as the market reprices 5-yr contract terms against 6-yr lives, without any funding failure. Ordinary 93%-vol noise reaches $52 more easily than in round 2. Round 4 leaves it at $48: the site work lifts the floored DCF only from $0 to ~$5 and the multiple from 5.1x to 5.2x, and it adds a stranded-lease channel through which a delivery failure would reach the equity faster.

key_uncertainties: Post-contract re-contract price: ~50% of original (base) vs ~95% (tight). This moves the base-cell DCF from -$74 to +$19 a share at 2.6x.
Capex intensity on new capacity (2.4-2.7x). Every evidence-consistent path still earns below WACC (cohort IRR rises only ~2 pts at a 25% site cost).
Signed vs contracted: ~$80B of signed revenue remains at Oct-27 against ~$157B of in-term revenue modelled on 4.2 GW. If the unsigned half re-prices lower or slips, the leases (12-15 yrs) still run.
Delivery: Helios II slipped ~1 yr, Poolside exited, DDTL 3.0 tests were reset to 2027-10-31; 2027 cohort timing (~1.1 GW) drives the >3 GW YE27 guide.
Funding cost and access for ~$20-25B of 2027 external capital: IG-contract loans at ~7% vs unsecured at 9-9.75%; CDS hit ~855bp in Jul-26.
Customer concentration (Customer A 36% of Q2 revenue) and unrated counterparties (OpenAI ~$16B, Anthropic) in ~38% of the signed book.
Dilution: 35M ATM, converts at $97.85/$107.80/$119.60, SBC ~5% of revenue.
reasoning: Round 4, skeptic lane. Two fixes. (1) Sites: I mapped all 45 inventory rows onto the cohort model, each once. Energized sites (1.85 GW at YE26, including ~857 MW at sites with undisclosed MW, allocated by judgment) form the <=2026 cohorts. Contracted sites under construction form the 2027 (~1.13 GW) and 2028 (~1.23 GW) cohorts, filling the 4.2 GW. Kenilworth and Hammond are self-builds with no disclosed customer, so they are probability-weighted (0.9/0.75) with shell capex charged and lease saved. The 1.5 GW of land/options/LOIs (P0.5) and the NVIDIA framework, counted only for the 2.3 GW gap to 8 GW (P0.2), replace round 3's certain 2029-30 adds. Poolside and the Core Scientific merger are removed. JV commitments ($1.37B) go into net debt. The inventory's lease rates ($1.44-2.2M/MW-yr) put the site cost at ~25%, not 28%. (2) Discounting: signed in-term cash is discounted at 8.6%. That is anchored on DDTL 4.0 (~5.9% fixed in Mar-26, ~6.9% at today's 3-yr Treasury, plus a first-loss residual) for IG counterparties at 8.0%; Jane Street is 8.75%; OpenAI, Anthropic and other unrated counterparties are 9.5% (DDTL 3.0 at S+400). Everything else stays at 11.5%. The skeptic finding is that contracted power is not contracted revenue: ~$80B of signed RPO remains at Oct-27 against ~$157B of in-term revenue modelled on the 4.2 GW, so only ~$36B of PV gets the lower rate. Results, base cell: -$128.9 -> -$74.2 (cost +$26.5, pipeline weighting +$22.7, site items +$2.6, split +$2.9). Single-rate -$77.1. Floored grid: $4.6 split vs $4.0 single (round 3 $0). Runoff floor: -$15 split, but -$62 once stranded rent on the 12-15-yr leases is counted (flag F8), so refresh is forced. EV/EBITDA: the installed-asset annuity rises to ~4.0x, giving 5.2x and $69. Fair value $36.8 (from $32.5). The 12-month price still follows the multiple, so I move the ladder only slightly: main-component median $81 -> $83, distress weight unchanged at 16% (stranded-lease risk offsets the IG-financing comfort); P(>=89) 0.380 -> 0.392. Scenarios: bear $34/30%, base $80/50%, bull $145/20%. Thesis break $48. 1-month ladder unchanged. Research this round: no web searches; one primary fetch (DDTL 4.0 deck, confirming SOFR+225 / ~5.9%, A3, 90% LTC, 1.2x DSCR) plus the inventory and fact-check files. No options data or priors/ files.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Contract price (1.00) for the 5-yr take-or-pay term; then 0.50 (yr 6) and 0.41 (yr 7) of the contract price, retired when below power+colo+maintenance (~0.33-0.37). Derived from a spot path relative to launch of 1.00/0.65/0.45/0.38/0.33/0.28/0.23 (steep for ~2 yrs after the next generation ships, ~-15%/yr after), with the 5-yr contract priced at the average of yrs 1-5 (0.56).
gpu_life.note: Basis: UNFLOORED per share at Oct-2027, k 2.6x, split rate (single-rate: -104.6/-77.1/-75.0). Floored, all three are $0. Tight path 19.3 at 2.6x, 37.7 at 2.4x. Runoff: 5y/6y/7y -$21/-$15/-$15 without stranded rent, -$77/-$62/-$54 with it. Fact-checked company lives: CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5 (from 1 Jan 2026), IREN 5. The 6-yr base matches the book life. At 25% fixed cost the cash rule gives 6-7 yrs. The life label is worth ~$30/share (5y vs 7y), against ~$93 between the base and tight paths.

site_coverage.site: PIPE-LAND Powered land, expansion options and executed LOIs
site_coverage.treatment: Uncontracted pipeline: probability-weighted run-rate adds at WACC, net of 2.6x capex (financing cost is in the WACC); same contract-then-decay economics as contracted cohorts.
site_coverage.note: 1.5 GW of powered land, options and LOIs. Sized as $15.5B of 2029 run-rate at P=0.5: the company counts it toward 8 GW, but it has no customer and needs ~$40B of capex at a ~9% parent funding cost (CDS ~800bp in Jul-26), and Poolside shows such capacity can vanish. Negative because each cohort earns below WACC, so a lower probability raises value.

site_coverage.site: PIPE-NVDA NVIDIA collaboration framework (>5 GW of AI factories by 2030)
site_coverage.treatment: Uncontracted pipeline: probability-weighted run-rate adds at WACC, net of 2.6x capex (financing cost is in the WACC); same contract-then-decay economics as contracted cohorts.
site_coverage.note: NVIDIA >5 GW framework overlaps the 8 GW target and the contracted/pipeline MW. Only the 2.3 GW gap from 5.7 GW (contracted + land) to 8 GW is counted: $23.7B of 2030 run-rate at P=0.2 ('subject to future agreements'). Reconciliation (base cell: 6-yr life, k 2.6x, split rate): site rows sum to $43.5/share of EV; post-2030 growth convention (3% of active capacity, not a site) $-13.9; net debt incl. JV commitments $64.37B = $103.8; equity $-74.2/share unfloored. The floored, probability-weighted grid gives $4.6.

discounting.basis: Contracted rate applies to the signed share of in-term cash flows only (~$80B of signed revenue remaining at 2027-10-01; ~$36B PV). IG counterparties (Meta Aa3/AA-, NVIDIA Aa1/AA, Microsoft Aaa; ~55%) at 8.0%. Anchor: DDTL 4.0 non-recourse loan against the IG contract at SOFR+225 / ~5.9% fixed (A3, 90% LTC, 1.2x DSCR; deck read), re-struck to ~6.9% for the 3-yr Treasury's rise from 3.81% to 4.91%, plus a ~17% first-loss residual at ~13% for completion and operating risk. Jane Street (Fitch BBB-, Moody's Ba1, S&P BB; ~7%) at 8.75%. Unrated OpenAI/Anthropic/other (~38%) at 9.5%, from DDTL 3.0 at SOFR+400 (~8.1%) plus residual and concentration. Blend 8.6%. Unsigned in-term cash, post-contract tails, refresh, pipeline, growth and terminal value stay at the 11.5% WACC. Floored grid DCF: single 4.0 vs split 4.6. Unfloored base cell (6y, 2.6x): single -77.1 vs split -74.2. The split adds ~$2.9/share, ~0.14 of NPV per $ of signed run-rate. Reconciliation (base cell: 6-yr life, k 2.6x, split rate): site rows sum to $43.5/share of EV; post-2030 growth convention (3% of active capacity, not a site) $-13.9; net debt incl. JV commitments $64.37B = $103.8; equity $-74.2/share unfloored. The floored, probability-weighted grid gives $4.6.
